newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia Kovinotehna 96 profit sharply up.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia Kovinotehna 96 profit sharply up.

text.p: Slovenian trader Kovinotehna on Wednesday posted a rise in 1996 net profit to 248.8 million tolars ($1.5 million) from 14.3 million the year before, but said it would not pay a dividend.
Sales rose to 33 billion tolars from 26.2 billion in 1995.

"Shareholders decided to pay no dividend in order to increase reserves because they considered that would be best for the company," deputy chief executive Milena Sedovnik told Reuters. Kovinotehna did not pay a dividend last year either.
The company said profit was up due to improved organisation, lower costs and an increase in trading with the former Yugoslav republics.
By 0915 GMT ordinary shares of Kovinotehna were unchanged at 490 tolars, while preferred shares were up 4.44 percent to 470 tolars.
Traders said gains could be expected from the firm's shares due to good business results and predicted that the ordinary shares could reach 535 tolars by end July.
